glosses: talisman, amulet, mascot
предмет, который, по суеверным представлениям, приносит его владельцу счастье, удачу, избавляет от болезней, опасности, беды

examples.text: Валяются полётные карты, пилотские шлемы, пластмассовый жёлтый утёнок — талисман, оберегавший лётчиков от беды.

glosses: A magical object providing protection against ill will, or the supernatural, or conferring the wearer with a boon such as good luck, good health, or power(s).

examples.text: That woman’s love is a talisman by which he holds and hopes to get his safety.
I have in my possession three Magic Talismans, which I have ever guarded with utmost care, keeping the knowledge of their existence from anyone else.
Dagobert gave him back his passport. He re-pocketed it indifferently; a talisman which had lost its potency.
She kept low, clutching the rifle she'd taken as though it were a magic talisman, as if it would somehow protect her even though she didn't fire it.

Mata would soon whip in the cross that allowed Drogba to equalise – and Chelsea went on to win the Champions League, beating the German club on penalties, with their talisman from the Ivory Coast making history with the final spot-kick.

glosses: To adorn with a talisman.

examples.text: The second in his saddle reeled, / Down thundered man and horse;— / Oft I essayed with blow and thrust, / As oft a foeman rolled in dust; / But, ah, what could a single arm, / Though talismaned by beauty’s charm, / Against a host?—for love—for life— / I waged awhile the desperate strife; / ’T was vain—I fell—was left for dead— / And rescued was th’ unwilling maid!
Lo, under their coats, amulets of idols! Possibly such charms talismaned every breast in his army.

They had a pitched battle in the spirit; the girl at length said, “You have something strong which I cannot endure,” and Madame Guyon confesses that she was talismaned by a piece of the true cross around her neck.

Fond youth, vain were thy sulphurous bolts against / This subtle necromancer, armed and talismaned / By the Grail’s prophylactic power.
It is yours still, and I go talismanned / By you to find you, though I’m lost & late.
And for that moment I believe her, am transformed, / Talismanned by carved jade beads, / For that moment I know she has / The word from God direct.

glosses: A mullah (Islamic religious scholar).
Something thought to bring good luck.

examples.text: I keep this red stone as a lucky mascot and always put it on my desk in exams.

glosses: Something, especially a person or animal, used to symbolize a sports team, company, organization or other group.

examples.text: Tommy the Tyke is the mascot of Barnsley FC.

glosses: A person engaged by an organization to portray its mascot in costume.

examples.text: He's been working as a mascot at local hockey games.

glosses: A personality type characterized by reliance on humor and positivity to wish away conflicts and attempt to defuse potentially violent situations.
To act as a mascot (for).

examples.text: The seniors were “mascoted” by two little girls dressed in green dresses […]
Unlike the popular, sunny Van Zelst, McLoon was a sassy, hard-boiled kid who had been mascoting for various athletic teams and prize fighters […]
Bennett then signed with the Brooklyn Dodgers, whom he mascoted to the 1921 pennant and two wins in the first three games of the World Series, which were played at home.

glosses: A religious article, protective charm, or ornament, usually bearing cultural or magical symbols, worn for protection against ill will, negative influences, or evil spirits.

examples.text: The soldier wore an amulet for protection.
An ancient amulet was discovered in the ruins.

glosses: Objeto portátil al que se atribuyen virtudes mágicas.

examples.text:

glosses: Persona, objeto o animal considerado como portador de buena suerte.
Personaje, generalmente no humano, que hace de emblema y representa un grupo de personas o una institución. Frecuentemente aparece en eventos, competencias o certámenes.
Animal doméstico o de compañía.
Sombrero flexible.
Gegenstand, der Unheil abwenden beziehungsweise Glück bringen soll

examples.text: Talisman in Karneol, / Gläubgen bringt er Glück und Wohl; / Steht er gar auf Onyx' Grunde, / Küß ihn, mit geweihtem Munde! / Alles Übel treibt er fort, / Schützet dich und schützt den Ort: / Wenn das eingegrabne Wort / Allahs Namen rein verkündet, / Dich zu Lieb und Tat entzündet. / Und besonders werden Frauen / Sich am Talisman erbauen. / Amulette sind dergleichen / Auf Papier geschriebne Zeichen.

glosses: Objet sur lequel sont gravés des figures, des signes, des caractères, auxquels on attribue des vertus magiques ou préservatrices.

examples.text: Le talisman, le remède tout-puissant.

glosses: Objet sacré protecteur.

examples.text: Puis, montrant la relique : − Voici de plus un talisman qui préserve des coups d'épée mieux que ne ferait une cotte de mailles.

glosses: Synonyme de phalène anguleuse.
Pièce maîtresse d’un objet qu’elle complète et achève.

examples.text: Bien avant d’acquérir une connotation merveilleuse, le mot « talisman » signifiait « achèvement ». Dérivé du grec telesma, « complet ».
